entry.title: BearBlog Best Practices: Avoiding Common Pitfalls
entry.summary: When I started automating blog posts to BearBlog, I thought it would be as simple as writing Markdown and sending it over. I was wrong. BearBlog's free plan has some quirks that can trip up even careful automation. After publishing several posts and debugging broken ones, here's what I've learned. BearBlog's CLI (bearcli.py) takes a markdown file and expects only the body—no YAML front matter at all. The CLI itself generates title, link, and published_date from the filename and current time. If you include YAML headers (--- delimiters with title, date, etc.) in your body file, BearBlog will literally render those lines as text at the top of your post. I learned this the hard way when my first few posts had raw YAML showing up on the live page. Fix: Write body-only markdown files. No title:…
